groundhog-removal.intro: North is a small Orangeburg County town on US-321 — named, as every local will tell you, for a railroad man and not the compass — standing in the flat-to-rolling farm country between Columbia and Orangeburg. Its groundhog work is the farm-belt standard: burrow systems in the field banks and road cuts, dens under the barns, sheds, and older homes' porches, and gardens raided at the town's edges where the fields meet the yards. The soil here — sand over clay — digs well and holds a tunnel, and a groundhog system on a good bank is a multi-year construction that its tenants improve every season it is left alone.
groundhog-removal.extendedBody:
Sand over clay: systems that last

A North groundhog burrow is not a hole; it is a system — main entrance with its spoil fan, plunge holes for escape, chambers below the frost line — and the work accounts for all of it. We trap the animals working the ground under the depredation permit for your property, then close the system: entrances in the active ground collapsed or screened, and any burrow that runs under a structure backfilled with the settlement risk in mind, because soil removed from under a slab edge is a bill that arrives later if it is ignored. The habitat read comes with the job — which banks on your ground are permanent groundhog real estate (sunny, drained, above forage) and which systems were one dispersing animal's trial — because in Orangeburg County farm country the question is never whether groundhogs exist nearby; it is whether your banks stay tenanted. February is the month to be ahead of the year: a system cleared before the young are born is a single job; the same system in May is a family.

faqs.q: How much does groundhog removal cost in North?
faqs.a: It depends on the system's size and what it runs under — a garden bank is one job; a system undermining a barn foundation is another, with backfilling in the quote. We walk the ground, count the active entrances, and give one firm price for the trapping and the closing together. Removal runs under a depredation permit issued for your property, arranged as part of the work.

faqs.q: Groundhogs keep raiding our North garden from the bank behind it. Will removing them end it?
faqs.a: Removing the residents and closing the bank's entrances ends the current tenancy — and the bank is the honest conversation. A sunny, well-drained bank above a garden is the best groundhog address in the neighbourhood, and dispersing animals will prospect it most springs. What changes the odds permanently is the closing done properly plus the bank's edge managed — brush and cover at the burrow line kept down so the site reads exposed. We will show you the entrances and the cover that makes them attractive, and the goal we quote for is seasons of quiet, not a promise the county is out of groundhogs.
